grader: Codex /root/formal_checks; independent of participant outputs, contributor to formal checker implementation
user_turn: Two machines each have port 8080, with different owners. Our claim is each port has exactly one owner. Does that prove the claim inconsistent? I have not yet defined what identifies a port in this theory.

grades.explanation: Explicitly asks which identity is intended and leaves port-identity open.

grades.excerpt: No. The observation only proves inconsistency under a specific reading of port identity, and you have not chosen one. If a port is identified by its number alone, then port 8080 has two owners and the claim fails. If a port is identified by machine plus number, these are two distinct ports with one owner each and the claim holds. So this is a potential conflict conditional on the missing identity definition, not a proof. I would record the claim, the observation, a potential-conflict hypothesis with that explanation, and an open condition-shaped question about port identity, and make the claim depend on that question. No accept, withdraw or resolve operations are proposed.
grades.explanation: Refuses unconditional proof of inconsistency; possible conflict is explicitly conditional on unspecified identity.
Does not ratify machine/number or number-only; both are alternatives in an open question and new claim remains proposed.

observations.detail: Identity question presents number versus machine/number only. Neither is accepted; a future interview should allow other keys instead of implying these exhaust all models.

scope: Judged isolated no-tool Fable proposals followed by separate real CLI application to temporary graphs. Not a tool-driven multi-turn interview, interactive retrieval, generalized correctness claim, or proof of graph benefit.
